references.text: The prophecy in Isaiah about light and glory that will come upon Israel can be seen as a precursor to the description of 'anatolē ex hypsous' (the sunrise from on high) in Luke, which symbolizes salvation and God's intervention.

Micah prophesies about a ruler from Bethlehem, 'whose origins are from old times, from days of old.' This can be seen as a parallel to 'anatolē ex hypsous' in Luke, representing a new beginning and salvation.
Malachi speaks of 'the sun of righteousness with healing under its wings.' This can be connected to 'anatolē ex hypsous' in Luke as a metaphor for healing and salvation that comes from God.
